text.arabic_uthmani: وَإِن نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلَا صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ

words.gloss_range: connective opening that carries the prior transport-sign discourse into the conditional warning

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: conditional particle fused after the opening connective

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the ayah begin as continuation, not as an isolated threat. The same discourse that has just named created conveyance is carried forward into possible drowning, so mercy and risk stay grammatically adjacent. In the fused wa-in opening, connection and contingency arrive in one first beat.

topics.headline: transport mercy remains linked to risk
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the drowning threat grows out of the transport-sign discourse rather than starting a detached scene.
topics.reason: QAC reads the opening as a conjunction, and the following conditional clause keeps the warning syntactically tied to the prior discourse.

topics.headline: connection and condition fuse at the start
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the warning's first audible unit already combines linkage with contingency.
topics.reason: The surface segmentation places the prefixed connective directly on the conditional particle.

words.gloss_range: live conditional particle governing the jussive will clause and keeping the disaster sequence within conditional scope

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: jussive will and drowning sequence governed by the condition

words.prose: {{ar:إِن}} ({{tr:in}}) frames the scene as live contingency. It governs the jussive pair {{ar:نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ}} ({{tr:nashaʾ nughriqhum}}), so drowning and the following rescue-denials remain consequences inside one conditional architecture. Because it is fused after the preceding connective, the condition enters as a connected warning rather than as a neutral hypothesis.

topics.headline: condition keeps the disaster sequence scoped
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that drowning, no responder, and non-rescue are threatened consequences, not an unconditional report.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the protasis and apodosis as a forced conditional chain and warns against detaching the rescue denials from that scope.

topics.headline: conditionality enters through the connective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the particle is both grammatical condition and warning speech-act at the ayah boundary.
topics.reason: The input aligns the particle as the second segment of the fused opening and as the governor of the jussive sequence.

words.gloss_range: divine willing in a conditional jussive frame, with the willed content supplied by the following drowning verb
words.root_gloss_range: will, volition, and determinate outcome; local grammar selects willing as the conditional control point

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following verb supplies the content of the willing

words.prose: {{ar:نَّشَأْ}} ({{tr:nashaʾ}}) is the will-clause under the conditional particle, clipped into the jussive rather than standing as an independent statement. The verb names divine volition while leaving the object of willing compressed; {{ar:نُغْرِقْهُمْ}} ({{tr:nughriqhum}}) immediately supplies the threatened content. The final hamza gives the will-clause an audible stop before the drowning verb, matching the threshold from volition to enacted submersion. The root field {{ar:ش ي أ}} ({{tr:sh-y-ʾ}}) makes the disaster a governed outcome, and the same-surah recurrence of willing in power-threat frames (36:47; 36:66; 36:67) keeps this word as a control point for reversal.

topics.headline: conditional jussive makes will the protasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine willing is grammatically framed as the condition that governs the threat.
topics.reason: The verb is a first-person plural jussive under the conditional particle, with no overt object of will.

topics.headline: will precedes physical submersion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the visible danger is governed before it becomes physical.
topics.reason: The root's volitional force and the local word order place divine willing before the drowning verb.

topics.headline: same-surah will frames reversals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a local surah pattern in which divine willing can reverse assumed securities such as transport and sight.
topics.reason: CRITICAL rows cite same-surah uses at 36:47, 36:66, and 36:67, and broader divine-will parallels at 76:30 and 81:29.

topics.headline: final hamza marks the threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an audible stop between willing and enacted drowning.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the surface form and reinforces the transition into the next verb.

words.gloss_range: caused drowning or submersion of the same plural group, inside the conditional answer
words.root_gloss_range: drowning, sinking, engulfment, and broader images of complete immersion; local Form IV selects caused submersion

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: will, no responder, and non-rescue frame the drowning verb

words.prose: {{ar:نُغْرِقْهُمْ}} ({{tr:nughriqhum}}) is not the sea acting on its own. Its first-person plural morphology keeps divine agency in the verb, and the attached 3mp suffix makes the threatened group the direct object of caused submersion. The root {{ar:غ ر ق}} ({{tr:gh-r-q}}) releases the water-risk latent in the prior transport scene: the conveyance benefit can become engulfment. The accepted intensified reading nugharriqhum sharpens that pressure as a variant, while the local surface remains Form IV caused drowning. The heavy back-to-stop sound texture, from ghayn toward qāf, reinforces the sense of being enclosed and cut off under water.

topics.headline: divine causation acts on the plural object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that drowning is caused upon the same group, not merely experienced as environmental danger.
topics.reason: Attachment and valency evidence identify a first-person plural Form IV verb with a clitic direct object.

topics.headline: transport space becomes engulfing water
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior riding mercy carries its own hidden water-risk.
topics.reason: V4 supports drowning and engulfment branches, but local grammar selects caused water-submersion rather than every extended immersion branch.

topics.headline: variant thickens the causative drowning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that an accepted variant can intensify the same threatened drowning without changing who is threatened.
topics.reason: The variant evidence sharpens causation, while the aligned local form remains Form IV in the main surface.

topics.headline: ordinary riding is shadowed by judgment drowning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a familiar judgment-root can shadow ordinary human conveyance with the same drowning possibility.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete drowning parallels at 2:50 and 17:69, and the local context supplies the maritime setting.

topics.headline: sound texture reinforces enclosure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb's sound is heard as heavy enclosure at the moment of submersion.
topics.reason: The sound rows are local observations about the pronounced form and support the drowning image without changing the lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: consequential connector introducing the no-responder result after the drowning clause
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge from submersion to aftermath. It makes {{ar:لَا صَرِيخَ}} ({{tr:lā ṣarīkha}}) follow as the immediate consequence of the drowning condition, not as a detached moral generality. In the fused fa-la form, consequence and negation arrive together.

topics.headline: drowning entails the no-responder aftermath
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the lack of responder is the result of the drowning scenario, not a separate maxim.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following no-responder clause as the result after the drowning apodosis.

topics.headline: result and negation share one surface beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first rescue denial is introduced without a pause after the result marker.
topics.reason: The surface token binds the result connector directly to the first negation.

words.gloss_range: genus-negating particle before the accusative indefinite noun, denying the responder class

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accusative indefinite noun governed by genus-negating negation

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) here is the genus-negating negation before {{ar:صَرِيخَ}} ({{tr:ṣarīkha}}). It does not merely say that one helper fails; it empties the whole responder category for the threatened group. Its later repetition before the passive clause creates a second negative beat, so the ayah first deletes the helper class and then deletes the rescue process.

topics.headline: whole responder class is negated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar removes the category of responder, not only a single possible helper.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following noun as the governed complement of genus-negating negation.

topics.headline: first negation prepares the second
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the layered denial: no responder exists, and no extraction occurs.
topics.reason: The two local negations target different clause types, preserving both category-loss and process-loss.

words.gloss_range: rare negated noun spanning cry, crier, responder, and helper within an emergency-response frame
words.root_gloss_range: raised cry, cry for help, and answering with aid; unrelated nominal branches are not active locally

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: categorical negation specified for the threatened group

words.prose: {{ar:صَرِيخَ}} ({{tr:ṣarīkha}}) is the word on which the first rescue denial concentrates. As an accusative indefinite under the genus-negating particle, it is categorically erased. Its root {{ar:ص ر خ}} ({{tr:ṣ-r-kh}}) ranges across alarm, cry for help, and answered aid, so the negation collapses the emergency exchange at both ends: no effective cry-channel and no responder. That range is local to distress-response here; unrelated lexical branches do not enter the ayah. The same root field also recalls mutual rescue denial and clamoring distress (14:22; 35:37), while the word's rarity and rough sound make one noun carry the burden of a whole failed response system.

topics.headline: case and indefiniteness erase the class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one singular indefinite noun under negation erases the whole responder role.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by genus-negating negation as an indefinite accusative complement.

topics.headline: cry and answer fail together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied word covers both the distress signal and the responder/helper side of the emergency exchange.
topics.reason: V4 supports cry, help-seeking, and aid-answering branches, while local context narrows the range to distress-response rather than unrelated senses.

topics.headline: root echoes helpless exchange
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the drowning scene borrows a Quranic no-rescue exchange rather than using a generic helper word.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite concrete root parallels at 14:22 and 35:37, which fit the local no-response scene without overriding the local grammar.

topics.headline: rare rough noun bears the denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a scarce, strained-sounding noun carries the whole emergency-response denial.
topics.reason: Contextual evidence marks the exact form as low occurrence, and the sound rows are local to the surface.

topics.headline: benefit becomes helpless exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same transport benefit becomes a scene where the riders have no distress-response system.
topics.reason: The pronoun chain and boundary rows keep the same threatened group from conveyance into no-aid.

words.gloss_range: prepositional lām specifying availability, relation, or possession for the threatened group

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: plural pronoun governed by the preposition

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) specifies who lacks the responder: the bound prepositional phrase pins the erased responder noun to this same threatened group. The lām can carry relation, benefit, possession, and availability, and in negation that overlap matters: no responder belongs to them, reaches them, or is available for them. Its postposed phrase completes the negative nominal frame after the responder class has first been erased.

topics.headline: no responder is available for them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the no-helper claim is targeted to the threatened group, not left as abstract nonexistence.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the pronoun the complement of the lām and the predicate relation for the negated noun.

topics.headline: the delayed phrase completes the no-aid frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence: erase the responder class first, then specify whose access has vanished.
topics.reason: The lām is bound to the pronoun in the postposed phrase attached to the negated noun.

words.gloss_range: attached plural pronoun governed by lām, keeping the same threatened group as no-aid recipient

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: same plural referent across object, recipient, and later subject roles

words.prose: The attached {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) inside the bound prepositional phrase keeps the same people in view. They have already been embedded as the object of nughriqhum; now they become the recipients for whom no responder is available. This pronoun prevents the no-helper clause from drifting into a generic statement and prepares the later independent pronoun, where the same group is foregrounded as not rescued.

topics.headline: same group becomes no-aid recipient
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same plural group moves from being drowned to being denied aid without reidentification.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence ties the pronoun to the same threatened group and marks it as governed by the preposition.

topics.headline: attached form precedes later foregrounding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the grammatical role-shift from object of drowning to no-aid recipient and later non-rescued subject.
topics.reason: The pronoun is attached in the prepositional phrase here, while word 12 is an independent pronoun before the passive verb.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle introducing a second negated clause after the no-responder clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links the second denial to the first without collapsing them. After the earlier negation, it naturally reads with a nor-value, yet it remains coordination: first no responder is available, then they are not rescued. In the fused wa-la form, the conjunction restarts the negative cadence while preserving the difference between resource-denial and outcome-denial.

topics.headline: two different denials are cumulative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah closes both the helper category and the saving event while keeping them distinct.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates a second negated verbal clause with the previous no-responder result.

topics.headline: the second negative beat begins
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause arrives as a connected continuation with a renewed negative beat.
topics.reason: The surface form combines the coordinator with the second negation.

words.gloss_range: verbal negation before the passive rescue clause, denying the process of extraction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: fronted-pronoun passive clause negated by the second negation

words.prose: The second {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) changes the target of negation. It does not govern an accusative genus noun as the first one did; it negates the passive verbal clause {{ar:هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ}} ({{tr:hum yunqadhūna}}). The ayah therefore moves from no responder exists to no rescue happens, completing the disaster sequence after the alarm-response channel has already failed.

topics.headline: second negation denies rescue as process
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second negation removes the extraction event, not another helper category.
topics.reason: The second negation governs a passive verbal clause coordinated with the previous nominal no-responder clause.

topics.headline: category-loss becomes process-loss
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sequence of losses: engulfment, no responder, no extraction.
topics.reason: The repeated negation mirrors the first while changing its grammatical target.

words.gloss_range: independent plural pronoun foregrounding the same group before the passive rescue verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: passive verb whose plural marking already encodes the subject group

words.prose: This {{ar:هُمْ}} ({{tr:hum}}) is independent, even though {{ar:يُنقَذُونَ}} ({{tr:yunqadhūna}}) already carries plural passive subject marking. The extra pronoun brings the victims forward before the rescue verb lands. It also completes the pronoun chain: the same group is object of drowning, recipient of no aid, and now foregrounded subject of non-rescue while agency drains from the scene.

topics.headline: independent pronoun spotlights the victims
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the victims are made visible before the passive rescue process is denied.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the independent pronoun as the subject before the passive verb, even though plural agreement is already present.

topics.headline: one group crosses three grammatical roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same referent moving from acted-upon object to no-aid recipient to foregrounded non-rescued subject.
topics.reason: Cross-reference rows license continuity across the object suffix, prepositional pronoun, and independent pronoun.

words.gloss_range: Form IV imperfect passive denying that the group is rescued or extracted from peril
words.root_gloss_range: rescue, deliverance, extrication, and recovery from danger; local passive selects being rescued/extracted while leaving the rescuer unspoken

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: no responder precedes the fronted victims and passive non-rescue

words.prose: {{ar:يُنقَذُونَ}} ({{tr:yunqadhūna}}) is the ayah's final word, so the scenario lands on non-extraction. Its Form IV passive keeps the patients visible and suppresses the rescuer, after the no-responder clause has already denied any responder. The root {{ar:ن ق ذ}} ({{tr:n-q-dh}}) names rescue and pulling free from danger, so the negation is not vague lack of help but failed deliverance from submersion. Same-surah usage at 36:23 sharpens the shift from failed rescuers to unrecovered victims, while broader rescue scenes (3:103; 22:73) show the field's range. The ending holds the plural group in the final passive state: no alarm-response, then no extraction.

topics.headline: passive denies rescue while suppressing rescuer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the victims remain visible while the rescuing agent is grammatically absent.
topics.reason: The local verb is Form IV imperfect passive with the rescuing agent suppressed and the plural group encoded as subject.

topics.headline: rescue means extraction from peril
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denied action is decisive extraction from danger, not generic assistance.
topics.reason: V4 supports rescue, extrication, and recovery branches; local Form IV passive narrows the field to being rescued or extracted.

topics.headline: alarm-response and extraction both close
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the staged disaster chain: will, engulfment, no alarm-response, and no extraction.
topics.reason: The local sequence links the drowning root, the no-responder noun, and the final rescue verb as one emergency field.

topics.headline: same root shifts from failed rescuers to unrecovered victims
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the local passive closure resonates with other rescue-root scenes while changing the grammatical focus.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite concrete rescue-root comparisons at 36:23, 3:103, and 22:73, and the local passive keeps the comparison as contrast rather than controlling the parse.

topics.headline: final sound holds collective non-rescue
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah's last sound leaves the plural group in unresolved non-rescue.
topics.reason: The word is final, passive, and plural, so the closure position and cadence reinforce the non-extraction state.

topics.headline: transport benefit ends as unrecovered disaster
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that created transport is not denied as a gift, but its security is revoked under the condition.
topics.reason: Boundary rows and pronoun continuity bind the prior transport premise to the final passive non-rescue.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The volitional condition at word 2 governs the causative drowning at word 3, followed by coordinated denials of responsive aid at word 5 and extraction at word 9.
baseline_models.mechanism: A sovereign condition can turn exposure to water into fatal immersion; once it is activated, neither an answering helper nor an extracting rescue remains.

activation_trace.role: Volition supplies the initiating condition for the entire consequence.
Water-submersion supplies the lethal event governed by that condition.
An answering helper is the first denied route out of the event.
Extraction from a predicament is the second and final denied route.

changed_reading.before: A generic warning that they could meet danger at sea.
changed_reading.after: A conditional act of submersion is presented as terminal because both responsive aid and physical extraction are explicitly closed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The noun at word 5 stands between drowning and passive rescue and can span loud sound, a plea for aid, and the one who answers it.
baseline_models.mechanism: The verse compresses an emergency chain into one polysemous node: alarm, appeal, response, and then extraction. The paired negations disable both the communicative chain and its practical result.

activation_trace.role: The raised urgent voice supplies the signal emitted under catastrophe.
The same node supplies an appeal seeking aid rather than mere noise.
The answering side of the call supplies the absent responder.
Successful extraction is the practical endpoint that never follows.

changed_reading.before: No rescuer happens to be present.
changed_reading.after: The whole signal-to-response-to-extraction system fails: no cry becomes effective aid, and no aid becomes removal from danger.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The causative drowning at word 3 and passive rescue at word 9 form an engulfment-versus-extraction opposition.
baseline_models.mechanism: Drowning is read as the medium occupying the victim's whole available field. Rescue would require an outside hand and an edge across which the victim could be pulled, but the final negation denies that crossing.

activation_trace.role: Water filling a field supplies the saturation image.
Total occupation supplies the loss of any free margin inside the event.
Extraction supplies the missing movement from occupied field to outside safety.

changed_reading.before: Drowning means simply sinking beneath water.
changed_reading.after: Drowning becomes total capture by a medium with no remaining edge, foothold, or external extraction path.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier bodily restraint, barriers on both sides, and an enveloping cover establish a repeated closure topology. The focus ayah converts that topology into fluid engulfment, where neither an answering agent nor extraction can cross the boundary.

activation_trace.role: Engulfment occupies the field that the earlier closures progressively delimit.
The absent answering helper shows that the closed boundary is also socially impermeable.
A restraining collar fixes the body and removes ordinary maneuverability.
The doubled barriers close gaps before and behind.
An all-over covering changes two-sided blockage into enveloping closure.

structural_cues: 36:8 fixes the body at the neck, and 36:9 repeats a barrier before and behind before ending in lost sight.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies bodily restraint, bilateral barriers, total covering, and later engulfment; I infer one recurring no-exit mechanism. A live alternative is that the earlier closures remain cognitive or moral images unrelated to the physical drowning.

changed_reading.before: The drowning is an isolated nautical hazard.
changed_reading.after: The drowning is the fluid culmination of a surah-wide closure pattern in which body, path, perception, appeal, and extraction are successively sealed.

context_deltas.mechanism: An earlier will-harm-no-rescue sequence tests proposed deities and intercessors, while a later sequence denies their capacity to help. The focus denial therefore exposes the failure of claimed patronage, not merely the absence of a nearby bystander.

activation_trace.role: The responder sense makes the denied figure a putative patron who should answer distress.
Extraction defines the concrete service that every claimed patron fails to provide.
Volition supplies the same controlling condition around an episode of harm.
Harm supplies the deficit against which the patrons' usefulness is tested.
A joined intercessor supplies the relational mechanism expected to add effective help.
The direct rescue-root echo explicitly denies extraction by those proposed patrons.
Expected aid supplies the motive for adopting the alternative patrons.
Denied capacity removes even the patrons' ability to perform the hoped-for aid.
The repeated aid root turns hope into an explicit failure of assistance.

structural_cues: 36:23 and 36:43 share a volition, harm, and no-rescue sequence; 36:74-75 later turns expected divine substitutes into agents unable to help.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit parallels in volition, harm, intercession, rescue, and failed aid; I infer that the absent responder in 36:43 includes the collapse of patronage architecture. The noun can still denote any generic rescuer, so the social reading need not exhaust it.

changed_reading.before: No helper happens to answer the drowning victims.
changed_reading.after: Every delegated patron, intercessor, or substitute source of aid is exposed as incapable of answering and extracting them.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, one terrifying cry can still life, seize disputants, and gather everyone into presence. Against that effective cry, the focus ayah denies any effective cry or responder from the endangered side.

activation_trace.role: Urgent raised sound supplies the endangered side of the vocal contrast.
A terrifying cry supplies a sound that produces an immediate collective effect.
The stilling of life supplies the first demonstrated outcome of that cry.
The repeated terrifying cry supplies a second sudden intervention.
Seizure supplies the cry's capacity to take people while their activity continues.
The third repeated cry supplies the transition into universal assembly.
Gathering dispersed persons supplies the collective result.
Compelled presence supplies the destination of the gathering.

structural_cues: The formula of one cry recurs at 36:29, 36:49, and 36:53, placing 36:43's denied emergency voice inside a repeated sound-and-effect sequence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated cries and their outcomes; I infer an asymmetry between ineffective creaturely distress and an effective summons. If the focus noun is taken only as rescuer, the contrast shifts from two sounds to human assistance versus an effectual command.

changed_reading.before: The drowning scene is merely silent and unaided.
changed_reading.after: The scene marks a vocal-power asymmetry: endangered voices cannot effect rescue, while one authoritative cry elsewhere effects death, seizure, and assembly.

context_deltas.mechanism: Ordered swimming, celestial course, carriage in a ship, a filled load, and riding all display supported motion through a medium. The focus condition can reverse that support relation so that the medium no longer carries but wholly engulfs.

activation_trace.role: Volition supplies the switch between continued support and engulfment.
Submersion supplies the reversal of supported movement.
A celestial course supplies ordered containment without collision.
Swimming or running supplies self-propelled motion within a surrounding medium.
Bearing a visible load supplies the protective support relation.
The waterborne vessel supplies the immediate material carrier.
Full loading supplies the carrier's occupied capacity and collective stakes.
Riding supplies the human posture of relying on a created support.

structural_cues: The adjacent sequence moves from all swimming in a course, to carried descendants in a filled ship, to created mounts, and then immediately to conditional drowning.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the double use of the course-or-vessel root, swimming, carrying, filling, riding, and drowning; I infer that 36:43 reverses one support relation. A live alternative keeps the celestial and maritime courses as parallel signs rather than one material mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The ship protects people from an otherwise external danger called drowning.
changed_reading.after: Carriage itself is contingent: the same ordered medium that bears swimmers, riders, and a filled vessel can be switched into total engulfment.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate exception supplies the only interruption of drowning and failed rescue. That interruption is mercy, and its result is not permanent immunity but usable continuance bounded by a time.

activation_trace.role: Denied answering aid rules out an autonomous third-party source of survival.
Denied extraction establishes the outcome that the following exception interrupts.
Merciful care supplies the sole exceptional source of retrieval or preservation.
Extended preservation supplies the lived result of the exception.
A bounded occasion supplies the endpoint of the preserved interval.

structural_cues: 36:44 begins with an exception immediately after 36:43's paired rescue negations and ends by bounding continuance with a time.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an immediate exception, mercy, extended use, and a temporal limit; I infer that the exception changes failed rescue into a granted reprieve. Alternatively, mercy may name the rescue event without specifying how it interrupts drowning.

changed_reading.before: Someone may still rescue them despite the verse's threat.
changed_reading.after: Any survival is neither independent rescue nor permanent safety; it is merciful retrieval or preservation granted only as a timed reprieve.

context_deltas.mechanism: Later repetitions of the same volitional formula remove sight, bodily form, capacity, forward motion, and return. The focus denial of aid and extraction is therefore one instance of a broader capacity-cancellation mechanism.

activation_trace.role: Volition governs the focus ayah's removal of safe passage through water.
Extraction is the exit capacity explicitly denied in the focus.
The repeated volitional form applies the same switch to vision.
Erasure of light and sight removes perceptual access to a route.
Ordinary visual capacity supplies the faculty made unusable.
A second repeated volitional form applies the switch to body and movement.
Transformation of bodily form removes the stable agent that would move.
Capacity itself is the resource explicitly canceled.
Forward passage supplies one unavailable direction of escape.
Return supplies the opposite direction, which is also unavailable.

structural_cues: 36:66-67 repeat the same if-We-will formula and conclude respectively with an inability to see and an inability either to proceed or return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated conditional and canceled faculties; I infer that 36:43 belongs to the same no-exit grammar. The alternatives are separate demonstrations of power rather than components of one shared mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The victims lack only an external helper.
changed_reading.after: The event closes an entire field of agency: perception, bodily maneuver, forward motion, return, responsive aid, and extraction can all be made unavailable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing formulation lays out a causal sequence from authority, to willing a thing, to saying, to occurrence. It turns the focus conditional from uncertainty about ability into a statement that the event remains contingent solely on activation by will.

activation_trace.role: Volition is the conditional switch whose force the closing sequence explains.
Command supplies the authoritative frame for execution.
Willing supplies the initiating state in the explicit causal sequence.
The knowable thing supplies a determinate object for volition.
Utterance supplies the mediating act between will and realization.
Occurrence in time supplies the realized endpoint of the sequence.

structural_cues: 36:43 has a compact condition-and-result construction; 36:82 expands willing a thing into saying and immediate occurrence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the ordered grammar of will, utterance, and occurrence; I supply the causal arrow that reads it back into 36:43. The closing formula can also remain a general creation claim rather than a specific gloss on drowning.

changed_reading.before: If-We-will sounds like an uncertain or merely hypothetical possibility.
changed_reading.after: The conditional marks executable dependence: drowning is unrealized only while volition does not activate it, and no counter-agency appears once it does.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The activation is surprising because 36:8 describes restrained posture, not a drowning scene, yet its branch inventory specifically supplies a raised-head-from-water image and the focus supplies actual immersion. It remains anchored to the drowning and extraction terms, but downstream prose should present it as a latent spatial resonance, not as proof that 36:8 secretly narrates water.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The drowning at word 3 and denied extraction at word 9 make head position relative to a waterline materially consequential.

activation_trace.role: Submersion supplies the waterline against which head position matters.
Extraction supplies the absent act that could restore the body above the waterline.
A raised head held away from water supplies an unexpectedly precise survival posture.
The collar supplies the constraint that fixes rather than freely achieves that posture.

changed_reading.before: Drowning is described without any prior bodily geometry.
changed_reading.after: A latent raised-head waterline image makes the focus threat bodily precise: survival depends on maintaining an airway position that engulfment and absent extraction can erase.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: The activation is surprising because the focus volition root and the later origination root are etymologically distinct despite their surface-near forms. It remains valid as a whole-surah sound-and-form trigger, especially beside the explicit will-to-occurrence sequence in 36:82, but downstream prose must call it paronomastic resonance and never a root derivation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The volitional form at word 2 is the phonetic and functional hinge that governs whether drowning occurs.

activation_trace.role: Volition supplies the focus form whose sound is reactivated later.
Origination supplies a root-distinct but surface-near image of bringing a thing into existence.
Explicit willing confirms the functional side of the resonance without collapsing the two roots.
Occurrence supplies the endpoint that links volition conceptually to origination.

changed_reading.before: The focus conditional expresses abstract preference over an already available event.
changed_reading.after: As a contained sound resonance, volition sits beside origination and occurrence: the drowning event itself depends on the agency that first brings things into being.

strongest_changes: The immediately preceding carrier sequence turns drowning into a reversal of an actively sustained support relation.
The following mercy exception recasts any survival as a bounded reprieve rather than autonomous rescue.
The earlier and later failed-patron passages make the absent responder an exposure of intercession and patronage systems.
The three effective single cries create a sharp contrast with the endangered side's ineffective emergency voice.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah ordering linked the focus's volition, drowning, cry, and rescue roots to repeated conditionals, supported motion, failed patrons, timed mercy, canceled capacities, and effectual cries; branch detail also exposed a waterline posture and a contained root-distinct origination echo.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus noun can emphasize a cry, a caller, or an answering rescuer, so the vocal-power model should preserve all three possibilities.
The celestial course and maritime vessel may function as parallel signs rather than one continuous support mechanism.
The origination echo is root-distinct and can carry sound-pattern activation only, not etymological argument.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The carrying medium can become the engulfing medium.** `ش ي ء` B002 supplies will toward a thing; `غ ر ق` B001 sinking in water; `ص ر خ` B002 a cry for help and B003 answering with aid; `ن ق ذ` B001 rescue. After safe carriage, a change in will reverses water from support to destruction and removes both call-answer and escape. I infer that safety lies not in the medium itself but in sustained permission. The ayah reads as contingency embedded inside technology.
2. **No answering cry reverses the single decisive cry.** The negated `ص ر خ` B003 aid contrasts with `ص ي ح` B002 in 36:29 and later 36:49, where a cry overtakes people. I infer an acoustic asymmetry: human cries cannot compel rescue, while the decisive cry effects transition. The ayah limits vocal agency.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 36:49's cry that takes people mid-dispute reinforced the asymmetry between being seized and securing rescue; the supposedly waiting subject is repeatedly made the event's object.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The carrying medium can reverse into total immersion.** **ش ي ء B001**, in its accepted “willing” variant, anchors **نَّشَأْ**; **غ ر ق B001** anchors sinking; and **ن ق ذ B001** anchors extrication. The packet has just supplied ship and ride as successful elevation over a medium (36:41–42). The inferred arrow is *continued carriage is contingent; withdrawal of enabling order lets the same surrounding medium take over the carrier's whole field*. Drowning reads as relational reversal, not an independent hazard.
2. **A cry exists but no answering aid.** **ص ر خ B002** supplies a cry for help and **ص ر خ B003** the answer with aid in **صَرِيخَ**. The negation can therefore retain both caller/helper scopes without choosing between them: neither help-call nor effective answer alters **لَا ... يُنقَذُونَ**. The packet supplies the doubled negative; the inferred mechanism is *communication cannot bridge a collapse once the preserving relation is withdrawn*. This prepares the contrasting mercy of 36:44.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: **Later surprise.** 36:44 immediately supplies the sole exception as mercy and prolonged benefit. This corrects a terminal reading of drowning: rescue is impossible from within the collapsed system, yet preservation can still arrive from outside it.

Borç, bela veya nimet içinde çıkışsız kalma, suyun altında kalmaya benzetilen bir kapsam genişlemesidir.
Boğulmak üzere olanın yakarışı, yalnızca belirli bir söz öbeğinde çaresizce yardım dileme anlamı taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki açık gerçekleşmeyi bir araya getirir: toprağın sulanmada en ileri doygunluğa ulaşması ve gözün yaşla dolması. Göz için özellikle yaşların henüz dışarı taşmaması kaydedildiğinden dal, her türlü akma ya da taşma değil, su veya yaşla dolma sonucu olarak sınırlandırılmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Toprakta suya doymuşluk, gözde ise dışarı akmayan yaşla doluluk vardır; gerçek boğulma ve serbest akış bu dalın çekirdeği değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, toprağı niteleyen biçim ile gözün yaşla dolmasını bildiren söz öbeğini ayrı gerçekleşmeler olarak korur.

concept_map.definition: Toprağın sulanarak suya bütünüyle doyması veya gözün yaşla dolup yaşları henüz dışarı akıtmamasıdır. Ortak sonuç, ilgili yüzey ya da boşluğun su veya yaşla dolmasıdır.

facets.statement: Bir yerin veya organın su ya da yaşla dolarak doygun duruma gelmesidir.
Toprak için kullanım, sulamanın en ileri derecesine ulaşmış ve suya doymuş araziyi anlatır.
Göz için kullanım, gözlerin yaşla dolmasını fakat yaşların henüz dışarı taşmamasını anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar toprağın yoğun sulamayla suya doyması ile gözlerin yaşla dolmasını aynı doluluk görüntüsünde birleştirir. Göz kullanımında yaşın oluşması yeterlidir ve bir anlatım, yaşların dışarı akmadığını ayrıca sınırlar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Göz ve toprak için ayrı sözlüksel gerçekleşmeleri ortak doluluk sonucu altında birlikte özetler.

error_profile.preserves: Doluluk çekirdeğini, sıvı türünü ve göz ile toprak arasındaki iki uygulama alanını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yaşların gözlerde biriktiği, özellikle henüz yanaklara akmadığı anlatımlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gözün yaşla dolmasını ve yaşın dışarı taşmaması sınırını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Sulamanın toprağı en ileri doygunluk derecesine ulaştırdığı arazi bağlamında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Toprağın suyla dolarak yüksek sulanmışlık derecesine ulaşması sonucunu korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: gözlerin yaşla dolması, fakat yaşların dışarı taşmaması

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yayı veya oku çekişin ulaşabileceği son sınıra kadar götürmeyi ortak biçimde anlatır. Bir anlatım çekişin ok üzerindeki belirli bölüme kadar sürmesini ayrıntılandırır; bu ayrıntı, genel çekme ya da ok atma değil, yay çekişinin tamamlanma derecesidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam yalnızca okçuluk yapısında yayın son sınırına kadar çekilmesidir; genel çekme, yayın denenmesi veya okun fırlatılması değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca yay çekme yapısına bağlıdır ve bu yapının son sınıra ulaşma koşulunu yalın kök anlamı gibi genelleştirmez.

concept_map.definition: Ok atmaya hazırlanırken yayı veya oku, yayın izin verdiği son çekiş sınırına kadar güçlü biçimde çekmektir. Belirleyici olan çekme eylemi değil, çekişin bütünüyle tamamlanmasıdır.

facets.statement: Yayı, çekilebileceği son sınıra kadar germek ve çekiş payının tamamını kullanmaktır.
Ok üzerindeki bağlama bölümünün yaya yaklaşmasına kadar süren şiddetli çekiş, işlemin teknik sınırını açıklar.
Yayı son sınırına kadar çekme görüntüsü, aşırılık ve ölçüyü kaçırma için atasözü niteliğinde de kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar okçunun yayı veya oku son çekiş noktasına kadar götürmesinde birleşir. Teknik ayrıntı, çekişin ok üzerindeki bağlama bölümüne kadar sürerek yayın bütün çekme payını tüketmesidir. Bu çekiş görüntüsü, aşırılık ve ölçüyü kaçırma için atasözü niteliğinde de kullanılır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca okçulukta, yayın çekiş payının bütünüyle kullanıldığı söz öbeğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yay bağlamını, çekme işlemini ve çekişin son sınıra ulaşması koşulunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Okçunun atıştan önce yayı mümkün olan en ileri çekiş noktasına getirdiği bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yayın çekilmesini ve çekişin tam sınırına ulaşmasını birlikte korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tek bir yalın anlamdan çok, yapıya bağlı iki düzen kurar: atın sürüye karıştıktan sonra onu geçmesi ve bir şeyin alanı bütünüyle kaplaması ya da tüketmesi. Nefes, bakış ve koşum takımı örnekleri ikinci düzenin farklı katılımcılar üzerindeki gerçekleşmeleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: At yarışı kullanımında karışma ve ardından geçme birlikte gerekir; öteki kullanımlarda ortak sınır bir alanı veya kapasiteyi bütünüyle kapsamaktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, at yarışı yapısını kapsama bildiren biçim ve söz öbeklerinden ayırır; hiçbir özel kullanım yalın kökün tek anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kullanımda atın öteki atların arasına karışıp ardından hepsini geçmesi, başka kullanımlarda ise bir eylem veya nesnenin ilgili alanı ya da kapasiteyi bütünüyle kaplamasıdır. Nefesi sonuna kadar verme, bütün bakışları üzerinde toplama ve gövdenin koşum takımına sığmayacak ölçüde büyümesi bu ikinci düzenin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir alanın, sürenin veya kapasitenin hiçbir pay bırakmadan bütünüyle kapsanmasıdır.
At yarışında atın sürüye karışması ve bu karışmanın ardından öteki atları geçmesi iki aşamalı bir kullanımdır.
Nefes kullanımında soluk verme sürecinin bütün kapasitesi sonuna kadar kullanılır.
Bakış kullanımında bir kişi insanların dikkat alanını tümüyle kendisine bağlayıp başkasına pay bırakmaz.
Koşum kullanımında hayvanın yanları ve karnı, göğüs ve karın kayışlarının çevreleyebileceği alanı bütünüyle doldurur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar atın öteki atlara karışıp sonra onları geçmesini ayrı bir yarış yapısı olarak verir. Kapsama düzeninde ise soluk verme bütünüyle sürdürülür, bir kişi bütün bakışları kendine çeker veya iri gövde koşum kayışlarının alanını doldurup onları dar bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi süt veya başka bir içecekten alınan küçük miktarda birleşir. Miktarın kabın üçte biri, bir küçük kap dolusu, bundan daha azı veya bir içimlik olarak açıklanması kesin bir ölçü değil, küçük içecek payının kaynaklara göre değişen örnekleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal bir içeceğin küçük sunum miktarını anlatır; kabın tümü, susuzluğu gideren büyük içiş veya kapta kalan tortu zorunlu değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın adın küçük süt veya içecek payı anlamıyla sınırlıdır ve başka dallardaki boğulma ya da yumurta anlamlarını içeri almaz.

concept_map.definition: Sütten veya başka bir içecekten, bir içimlik ya da küçük bir kap dolusu sayılabilecek az miktardır. Kaynaklardaki üçte bir kap, bir küçük kap veya daha azı açıklamaları yaklaşık miktar çeşitleridir.

facets.statement: Süt veya başka bir içecekten içmeye ayrılmış küçük bir miktardır.
Miktar bir içimlik, küçük bir kap dolusu, bundan daha azı veya kabın yaklaşık üçte biri olarak değişik biçimlerde açıklanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar sütü merkezde tutmakla birlikte başka içecekleri de kapsayan küçük bir içme payında birleşir. Verilen ölçüler bir içimlikten küçük bir kap dolusuna veya kabın yaklaşık üçte birine kadar değişir ve tek bir kesin hacim oluşturmaz.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesindeki iki tanım aynı yumurta bölümünü açıkça göstermemektedir: biri yumurtanın iç kabuğunu, diğeri yenilen beyaz kısmı bildirir. Dal tek sözlüksel birim olarak korunabilir, ancak iki açıklamayı özdeşleştirmeden kaynak değişkeleri olarak sunmak gerekir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Karşılık, yumurtanın iç kabuğu ile yenilen beyaz kısmı arasında kaynaklara göre değişir; dış kabuk veya yumurtanın bütünü değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnızca bu özel yumurta bölümü adına bağlıdır; biçimin kökün yalın anlamını temsil ettiği varsayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Yumurtanın içinde bulunan ve bir açıklamada iç kabuk, başka bir açıklamada yenilen beyaz kısım olarak tanımlanan özel bir bölümdür. İki açıklama kaynak değişkeleri olarak korunur ve tek bir dokuymuş gibi birleştirilmez.

facets.statement: Bir açıklama söz konusu bölümü yumurtanın dış kabuğunun altında bulunan iç kabuk olarak tanımlar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi başka birinin elinden veya bir sıkıntıdan çekip çıkararak kurtarma çekirdeğini açıkça verir. Aynı ifade, çeşitli eylem biçimlerinin bu anlamı taşıdığını ve kurtarma eyleminden etkilenen şeyin de kurtarılmış nesne olarak adlandırılabildiğini gösterir; bu nedenle dalın eylem ile sonuç nesnesini birlikte ele alan çerçevesi kanıtla uyumludur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, çıplak anlam çekirdeğindeki kurtarma eylemini türemiş eylem biçimlerinden ve kurtarılmış nesneyi belirten sonuç adından ayırır; herhangi bir özel söz öbeğine özgü anlamı genelleştirmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka birinin elinden ya da içine düştüğü bir sıkıntıdan etkin biçimde çekip çıkararak kurtarmaktır. Aynı anlam alanında, kurtarma eyleminin nesnesi kurtarılmış şey olarak da adlandırılır.

facets.statement: Bir özne, bir şeyi veya kişiyi başka birinin elinden ya da sıkıntılı bir durumdan çekip çıkararak kurtarır.
Eylem, kurtaran öznenin etkin müdahalesini ve kurtarılanın içinde bulunduğu bağdan veya güçlükten çıkarılmasını içerir.
Kurtarma eyleminin nesnesi, eylemin sonucu öne çıkarılarak kurtarılmış şey diye adlandırılabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, başka bir topluluktan alınmış atları, düşmandan kurtarılarak alınmış atları ve düşmandan geri kazanılmış zırhı aynı dar nesne-durumu çevresinde toplar. identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, her türlü kurtarma eylemini değil, başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış ya da kurtarılarak geri kazanılmış belirli at ve zırh adlandırmalarını kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, atlara özgü söz öbeklerindeki tekil ve çoğul kullanımları, tek başına kullanıldığında bir atı veya düşmandan geri alınmış zırhı belirtebilen addan ayırır; bu özel kapsam çıplak kökün genel anlamı sayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış ya da kurtarılıp geri kazanılmış nesnenin durumunu anlatan, özellikle atlar için tekil ve çoğul adlandırmalarda ve düşmandan kurtarılmış zırh için kullanılan özel bir anlamdır.

facets.statement: Nesne, başka bir topluluğun veya düşmanın elinden alınmış ya da kurtarılarak geri kazanılmış olma durumuyla nitelenir.
Tekil veya çoğul adlandırma, başka bir topluluktan alınmış ya da düşmandan kurtarılmış atlar için kullanılır.
Tekil ad, atların bir ferdini belirtebildiği gibi düşmandan kurtarılarak geri alınmış bir zırhı da belirtebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak anlatımı, başka bir topluluktan alınmış veya düşmandan kurtarılarak geri kazanılmış atların tekil ve çoğul adlandırmalarını verir. Aynı tekil adın düşmandan geri alınmış bir zırh için de kullanılabildiği belirtilir.

concept_gloss.text: başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan geri alınmış at ya da zırh
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın ortak nesne durumunu, atlara özgü adlandırmaları ve zırh uzantısını tek bir açıklayıcı karşılıkta göstermek gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alma ya da kurtarıp geri kazanma koşulunu ve at ile zırh kapsamını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Tek bir atın başka bir topluluktan alınmış olması öne çıkarıldığında doğal ve doğrudan bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Atın başka bir topluluğun elinden alınmış olma koşulunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Çoğul at adlandırmasını, özellikle düşmandan kurtarma vurgusunu ve zırh kullanımını kapsamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Birden çok atın düşmanın elinden kurtarıldığı ve alındığı bağlamlarda çoğul karşılık olarak kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Atların düşmandan kurtarılıp alınması işlemini ve çoğul nesne kapsamını korur.
error_profile.loses: Düşman dışındaki başka bir topluluktan alma durumunu, tekil atı ve zırh kullanımını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Adın at yerine düşmanın elinden kurtarılarak geri alınan bir zırhı belirttiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Zırhın düşmanın elinden kurtarılıp geri kazanılmış olma durumunu korur.
error_profile.loses: Başka bir topluluktan alınmış veya düşmandan kurtarılmış atlara ilişkin tekil ve çoğul kullanımları kapsamaz.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: bu atlardan biri; düşmandan kurtarılmış zırh

error_profile.preserves: Başkasından veya düşmandan alınmış bir mal olma yönünü kısmen korur.
error_profile.adds: Her tür savaş kazancını ve bu özel kurtarıp geri alma koşulunu taşımayan malları da kapsar.
error_profile.collision: Belirli at ve zırh adlandırmalarını genel savaş kazancı kategorisiyle karıştırır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış ya da kurtarılmış atlar ile düşmandan geri alınmış zırha özgü adlandırma bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Daha önce sahip olunmayan herhangi bir şeyi edinme, kazanma ve düşman dışındaki yollardan elde etme kapsamı vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: bir şeyi elde etme veya kazanma
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Başkasından ya da düşmandan bir nesnenin ele geçirilmesi ve yeni bir elde bulundurma durumunun doğması ortak alandır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, nesnenin başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış ya da kurtarılmış olmasıyla ve at ile zırh türleriyle sınırlıdır; komşu dal ise edinmeyi ve kazanmayı nesne türü ya da kurtarma koşulu aramadan geneller.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış atlara ve geri kazanılmış zırha özgü kalıplaşmış nesne adlandırmaları vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Herhangi bir şeyi veya kişiyi başka birinin elinden ya da sıkıntılı bir durumdan çekip çıkararak kurtarma eylemi genel olarak kapsanır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir nesnenin başkasının veya düşmanın elinden kurtarılması ve kurtarılmış sonuç durumuna gelmesi iki dalı bağlar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal, kurtarma sonucunu belirli at ve zırh adlarına daraltır; komşu dal ise nesne türünü sınırlamadan kurtarma eylemini ve genel kurtarılmış nesneyi anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Nesnenin başka bir topluluktan veya düşmandan alınmış ya da kurtarılmış at veya zırh olması belirleyicidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Ordunun veya yöneticinin yol üzerinde, hedefe varmadan ya da paylaşım öncesinde aldığı mal ve hayvanların zamanlama ve bölüşüm durumu belirleyicidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da askerî çatışma çevresinde elde edilen mal veya hayvanlarla ilişkilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal nesnenin kimden ve nasıl alındığına ve belirli nesne türlerine dayanır; komşu dal ise alınan şeyin sefer ve paylaşım sürecindeki konumuna dayanır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar karşılaştırıldı; yayımlanan komşular özel geri-alınmış nesne anlamını genel edinme, genel kurtarma ve paylaşım öncesi savaş malı alanlarından ayırır. Zırh, seçilmiş pay, alıkoyma ve silaha yönelme gibi diğer adaylar yalnızca nesne veya senaryo alanını paylaşır; özel alma ya da kurtarma koşuluna daha keskin bir sınır eklemez.
